correctness.rationale: For any n≥1, L,η>0, direct branch arithmetic gives a short 2-step corridor and a long (4n+1)-step corridor through a complete modular 4n-cycle (gcd(2n−1,4n)=1). Their disjoint towers have total length S, hence cover the four-IET. The return map is rotation by L modulo A. Its exact wrap count yields H_k=k−floor((x+kL)/A), and the original-time clock is t_k=(S/A)k+(4n−1)(x_k−x)/A. Uniform x makes the count two-valued at every k with the stated probabilities and variance; rational rotation order u+v, containing exactly v long and u short excursions, gives the least original-map period 2u+(4n+1)v. Direct λ realization produces every coprime u,v. The packaged checker passes 54 exact parameter cases, 3,456 direct first returns, 700 prime full-map periods and 180 moment checks; they supplement, not replace, the universal proof.

value.rationale: The intrinsic dynamical question is not only whether cap orbits are periodic or dense, but how many physical iterations each induced return costs and how its cumulative delay fluctuates. The answer distinguishes two exact excursion heights, gives every original-time least period across a natural geometric family, and proves that the k-return time has only two possible values with variance bounded uniformly in k, rather than the linear variance of independent renewal times. This is a motivated complete quantitative invariant of the specific embedded dynamical system; no larger extension to arbitrary ambient maps is assumed.
